claim_description: Freelancer Maya Chen delivered a complete logo design package (primary logo, wordmark, color palette, and usage guide) to Brightline Media Ltd. under a signed statement of work. Brightline confirmed receipt and viewed the deliverables, then refused payment, claiming the logo was not what they had envisioned. A revision request was only raised after the contractual deadline had passed.
claim_title: Unpaid $500 invoice for logo design package
claimant_evidence: Signed statement of work: "$500 on delivery, net-15" — payment due within 15 days of delivery, with no approval, satisfaction, or acceptance clause anywhere in the document.
Delivery confirmation email dated March 3 with download links to the full logo package (primary logo, wordmark, color palette, usage guide).
Read receipt showing Brightline opened the delivery email and downloaded the files within an hour of receipt.
respondent_evidence: Email from Brightline's marketing lead: "the logo isn't what we envisioned, we won't pay" — a subjective judgment citing no breach of any written spec or requirement in the SOW.
A revision request sent March 12, nine days after the March 3 delivery and past the contractual deadline — asking for a different color scheme and a different font.
